assessment: Post-rebuild, this 66-entry pool has one job: make the v2 99 stand up at a professional tier-4 table, and it can do that on exactly two axes — turn-protection for the verified lines (Grand Abolisher, Drannith Magistrate) and closing power off the non-combat axes (the Jace/Teferi walker package) to repair the wincon-access drop to 42.6% by t6. It still contains zero punisher-half cards, so no swap can directly raise the 39.6% two-piece rate; what the pool honestly buys there is engine-half redundancy that survives Farewell (Jace Beleren) where the artifact Mine-effects and punishers die together. The four v1 cuts sitting in the pool as spares were all correct cuts — including White Sun's Zenith, whose swap-back I evaluate and reject below — and stack 005's refutation of the mana-positive Kitten loop confirms there is still no infinite mana anywhere for the Ballista/Hangarback/Statuary trap package to sink. Five swaps, five distinct outs, floor 4 throughout.

swaps.when: Every pod holding instant-speed interaction — at a tier-4 table that is every pod; cast it the turn you commit to the second Approach, the 004/005 loop turn, or the punisher deployment, not before.
swaps.why: Stack 002's only loss window is opponents' instants on the second Approach cast, and Abolisher's text — opponents can't cast spells or activate artifact/creature/enchantment abilities during your turn — closes that window for two mana; Greaves' one v2 job is shielding Displacer Kitten from targeted removal, but shroud does nothing against the sweepers that actually kill Kitten at this tier and nothing on the commit turn that decides the game.

citations.quote: The window opens when your win attempt either can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for

swaps.when: Pods where commanders return to the command zone (your own Supreme Verdict, Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares guarantee this) or anything casts from exile or graveyard — cascade, flashback, foretell, adventures, Breach-style — i.e., most tier-4 tables; bench it only in the rare all-from-hand pod.
swaps.why: Opponents can't cast spells from anywhere but their hands: every commander your uncounterable Supreme Verdict wraths away goes to the command zone and stays stranded there, and every cascade or graveyard cast at the table is simply illegal — while Worn Powerstone is the slowest of nine rocks (enters tapped, taps for colourless in a list with 50 blue pips) whose delayed ramp arrives exactly when Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount starts paying the bill instead. Note the honest limit: commanders this deck bounces with Hullbreaker Horror or Cyclonic Rift go to hand and remain castable — the stranding case is wraths and exile removal, not bounce (see opens_lines).

swaps.when: Whenever two-piece assembly or Farewell exposure is the complaint — which after the rebuild is always; sleeve it for any pod running artifact mass removal.
swaps.why: Horn of Greed's trigger decays with the measured land-drop rate (57.1% at t5, 48.2% at t6) exactly when the engine must be online, while Beleren's +2 draws each player every turn unconditionally — feeding Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke hands and Heliod's discount — and as a planeswalker he is the only table-draw engine in either pile that survives the artifact sweep that takes Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell and both punishers in one card.

citations.quote: consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)
the linear deck needs redundancy that shrugs off three answers

swaps.when: The direct answer to the rebuild's known cost — wincon access down to 42.6% by t6; best in counter-heavy, removal-light pods where a resolved walker sticks and the maindeck X-draw suite is live.
swaps.why: Jace is a standalone draw engine at {1}{U}{U}{U} on a 36-blue-source base whose static turns the maindeck's own Stroke of Genius, Braingeyser or Mathemagics, self-targeted for X ≥ library, into a win that needs neither combat nor the 39.6% two-piece (line flagged in opens_lines, needs a stack scenario); Brass Infiniscope is a four-mana colourless rock whose cantrip only fires if an X-spell follows it that same turn, and stack 004's ledger showed it recasts mana-negative in the loop.

citations.quote: the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered; the median runs three cheap ones and closes from any board

swaps.when: Sweeper-rich tier-4 pods — and every game plan that includes casting your own Supreme Verdict, which v2 made a core line.
swaps.why: Both cards convert spell velocity into board presence, but the rebuild's own Supreme Verdict wipes Mentor's monk board along with everything else, while Pilgrim survives your reset, gains a loyalty counter on every draw (3-5 a turn under Alhammarret's Archive, Teferi's Ageless Insight and the Mine effects — arriving turn 5 and climbing out of burn range immediately), and his -2 Spirit grows on each draw into a clock the next wrath resets but his loyalty doesn't feel.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves

opens_lines.why_plausible: Stack 002's framing is that the second cast's only window is the stack; Abolisher forbids opponents casting spells during your turn, which would close that window entirely — but Abolisher restricts only spell casts and artifact/creature/enchantment activations, so an opponent channeling Otawara (an ability of a land card, activated from hand) can still bounce Abolisher or the win attempt's other pieces on your turn. Whether the window is truly shut, and against exactly what, needs a walkthrough.

Jace's static replaces the empty-library draw with a win, the maindeck X-draw suite self-targeted presents exactly that draw, and the v2 doublers change the arithmetic: Alhammarret's Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight double each draw, roughly halving the X needed to empty the library — but the interaction of Archive's draw-two replacement with Jace's win replacement mid-resolution, and what happens if Jace leaves the battlefield partway through the draws, is layered-replacement territory that must be walked through. Blue Sun's Zenith is the pool's backup fuel with a complicating shuffle-back clause; Laboratory Maniac is the redundant win clause.

The stranding package: commanders killed by Supreme Verdict or exiled by Path elect the command zone (CR 903.9), and Drannith makes casting from there illegal — a repeatable soft-lock on commander-centric pods. But the zone-election mechanics decide its real coverage: Hullbreaker Horror and Cyclonic Rift bounces go to hand, which Drannith does not stop, and hand/library moves have their own election rule. The prior sideboard analysis overstated this as stranding bounced commanders; the corrected claim needs the 903.9 walkthrough before it is played as fact.

Fraying Sanity counts cards put into the enchanted player's graveyard from anywhere this turn, and this deck forces cleanup-step discards from Fruition-bloated hands (stack 003's trim-to-7 subtlety) — but Fraying Sanity triggers at the beginning of the end step, before cleanup discards happen, so whether trimmed cards ever count (including via a repeated cleanup under CR 514.3) is a genuine open rules question that decides whether the curse doubles the punisher engine or misses it entirely.

A free Approach via Omniscience is still cast from hand, which the win condition requires, and Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount on a forced-draw turn plus the table-draw density can realistically pay {7}{U}{U}{U}; free countermagic from hand then defends the second cast. Unverified: cast-from-hand satisfaction under alternative costs, the win-check timing, and the honest cost — every X-spell in the deck resolves at X=0 when cast for free under it.

long_term_defaults.why: Every verified win this deck has — the 002 second Approach, the 004/005 loop turn, the 003 punisher deployment — is committed on its own turn, and two mana protects all of them; there is no tier-4 pod where you would rather be holding Lightning Greaves.

Command-zone recasts (your own Verdict and exile removal guarantee the zone) and non-hand casts appear in essentially every tier-4 game; a two-mana body that makes them illegal is live unconditionally, unlike the enters-tapped colourless rock it replaces.

The only true engine-half redundancy in the entire pool: a repeatable each-player draw for three mana that keeps feeding punishers and Heliod's discount after land drops fail, and the only Mine-effect on either side of the list that lives through an artifact sweep.

A fine standalone draw engine at {1}{U}{U}{U} on a 36-blue-source base, plus the deck's only wincon that rides the X-draw suite instead of combat or the two-piece — worth the slot even before the self-draw line is verified, and the correct answer to the 42.6% wincon-access number.

In a deck drawing 3-5 cards a turn under its own engines the loyalty snowball survives every sweeper including your own Supreme Verdict — the resilient version of the board presence Monastery Mentor builds and loses.

The swap-back is rejected: it duplicates Secure the Wastes' effect class at a worse rate ({W}{W}{W} on 22 white sources in a 50-blue-pip deck), and X vanilla 2/2s from a draw-go deck must survive a full turn cycle of three opponents plus every sweeper — including your own Verdict — before dealing a point; the wincon-access drop is better repaired by a new non-combat axis (Jace) than a second copy of the deck's weakest wincon class. Its shuffle-back recursion is the one virtue: sleeve it only in ultra-long attrition pods where wincons get stripped and Secure the Wastes has already been spent.
The v1 cut was right: seven mana for one steal, and its draw rider needs three permanents you don't own; the v2 additions (Archive, Kwain, Second Doctor) do more for the actual plan at lower cost.

The v1 cut was right: it pays off by dying, which this deck never volunteers, and its Squid rebuild is 1/1s at a table where that is not a clock — Temporal Pilgrim is the strictly better draw-payoff body.
The v1 cut was right: the worst of the pool's X-token spells — sorcery-speed Allies with no payoff in a list whose verified wins are all noncombat.

Still the best pure-value card in the pool — a second Sphinx's Tutelage that mills 8-16 per turn cycle under the doublers — but with Brass Infiniscope's slot now spent on an actual wincon, its remaining displacement targets are ramp and pillow pieces the tier-4 posture needs; first alternate if a slot opens, and sleeve it in attrition pods without graveyard decks.

Its static makes the second Approach uncounterable — real tech for a genuine counter-war pod — but it is seven mana for protection Grand Abolisher gives at two on the only turn that matters; sleeve it when the pod runs three-plus blue seats.
Redundant copy of Jace's win clause on a 2/2 that dies to any removal mid-draw; sleeve it only if the self-draw line verifies and the pod is light on creature removal — never ahead of Jace.

Stack 005 closed the last hope: the Kitten exit is a one-time +1 float capping terminal mana at 3, so Ballista tops out at X=1 for a single ping — there is still no infinite mana anywhere in this deck to sink, and the mana-neutral loop recasts it at X=0 into the graveyard.
Same arithmetic as Walking Ballista under the verified 004/005 ledger: X capped at trivial size, a zero-counter Hangarback dies leaving zero Thopters.

Improvise applies only to nonartifact spells — the loop casts Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, both artifact spells, so Statuary never touches the ledger; outside the loop, tapping a rock for improvise yields the same {1} its mana ability would.

Still the trap it was: reducing opponents' maximum hand size by seven makes them trim toward zero at cleanup, so they reach their punished upkeep empty-handed — it switches OFF Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Viseling, the deck's verified 003 clock.

Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount on a Forced Fruition turn can shave double-digit generic off the cost and the deck can flash it in — a genuine haymaker, but off-plan, and the arithmetic is uncomputed: goldfish explicitly does not model cost reducers.
Same discount logic as Emrakul with a weaker payoff: nothing here makes opponents sacrifice, so its second ability is nearly blank and Annihilator is a combat plan the deck does not have.

The Approach package is real if a scenario verifies it, but nine mana with no built-in protection is the one-spectacular-finisher shape that loses to a single answer, and every X-spell in the deck is dead at X=0 when cast for free under it.
Worth a slot only if the cleanup-discard timing question in opens_lines resolves favourably; on its face it deepens mill on one opponent while this deck's engines pressure all three.

Backup fuel for the Jace line and an instant-speed hand-filler into the punishers, but maindeck Stroke of Genius already holds the slot and the shuffle-back clause complicates the empty-library math; the same scenario that verifies the Jace line should cover it.
All three modes play and {U}{U}{U} is fine on 36 blue sources, but the maindeck counter suite is already seven deep at better rates; first replacement if the suite thins.
Fine rate, but the existing suite is deeper and cheaper; the exile clause is its one edge — sleeve it against recursion pods specifically.
Without shuffle density (the 99 offers Flooded Strand, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans) it rearranges more than it draws; every engine card it could displace does more.
Banned in Commander (settled last pass via cards.csv legal_commander) — it can never enter the 99; even were it legal, the opponent controls the repeats and stops precisely when it would profit you.
Good card, wrong queue: it competes with Temporal Pilgrim for the walker slot and gains far less from the deck's draw density; second alternate behind Teferi's Tutelage if a slot opens.
Her upkeep draw needs a creature to have entered last turn and the v2 goldfish shows a mean of 1.46 bodies by turn 6 — the trigger misses more turns than it hits.
Sorcery-only flash when Heliod's back face and Leyline of Anticipation grant broader flash already, and the Ring text is blank in a deck with no tempt sources.
Its five-lands condition is live in barely half of games by the measured land-drop rates (57.1% at t5), and Ancient Tomb already serves the colourless-burst job without ever being a dead draw.
Colourless-only in a deck with 50 blue pips; two life does not pay for the {U} it cannot produce.

gaps: Correction of the superseded v1 analysis: it claimed Drannith Magistrate strands commanders this deck bounces with Hullbreaker Horror or Cyclonic Rift — bounce goes to hand, which Drannith does not restrict; the corrected stranding case (wraths and exile removal into the command zone) is flagged in opens_lines and needs the CR 903.9 walkthrough before being played as fact.

No swap can be shown to move the wincon-access number: goldfish_targets.json counts only Approach of the Second Sun, Aetherflux Reservoir, Secure the Wastes and Mystical Tutor, so adding Jace, Wielder of Mysteries (or swapping White Sun's Zenith back) changes the measured 42.6% only after a curated target edit plus a goldfish re-run — recommend that follow-up once the swaps land.

The pool still contains zero punisher-half effects, so the 39.6% two-piece-by-t6 rate cannot be raised directly from the sideboard; engine-half redundancy (Jace Beleren) is the only available purchase.

The strategy corpus still has no sections on group-slug donation risk, blink value engines, or hand-size as an attack vector (per strategic_frame.gaps), so the Displacer Kitten and punisher-adjacent judgments above rest on oracle text and the verified stacks rather than citable principles.
Emrakul / It That Betrays castability under Heliod's discount remains oracle-text reasoning only — goldfish's stated assumptions exclude cost reduction.

Five candidate lines need resolve-stack runs before any is played as fact: the Abolisher 002-window closure (channel-land loophole included), the Jace/X-draw self-deck win under the Archive doubler, the Drannith command-zone stranding scope, the Fraying Sanity cleanup-discard timing, and the Omniscience free second Approach.
